catalog_quote: Kondic 2012:48: "1.2 Stress The main lexical HSF stress is regular, and commonly falls on the (first) long vowel (HSF stress seems to be attracted by a heavy syllable). If there is no long vowel in a word, then the accent is on the first short vowel. This rule has already been proposed by Larsen and Pike (1949) for San Luis Potosí Huastec. ['?uxum] uxum woman [manu'nu:l] manunuul yellow [ta'ta:?] tataa' you, 2sg ['tamup] tamup year ... In South Eastern Huastec two long vowels normally do not occur in one word. ... The personal markers that precede a verbal complex are never stressed. They are written separately from the word in order to show that they do not interfere with the stress rule." sweep_summary: One title-sweep item for Huastec: Hagberg 1993/2006, An autosegmental theory of stress (Glottolog 141035; the 2006 SIL e-Books 3 reissue of the 1993 Arizona dissertation). The full text was already on file in this audit (archive.org item an-autosegmental-theory-of-stress, in the capa1241 folder) and was copied into with a extracted text layer and a line; PDF pages 199-200 were viewed as images to verify the accent marks. Hagberg treats Huastec (Larsen & Pike 1949 data, Potosino) as unbounded quantity-sensitive: stress on the rightmost long vowel, else the first vowel (WSP right-to-left + End Rule Left, no feet, word domain), with 12 forms in (82). This confirms the catalog's 'weight' coding and the rightmost-long-vowel reading the catalog prule already carries for Potosino; it is second-hand, so it does not supersede Kondic 2012:48 as the deciding first-hand source. Its rendering of Larsen & Pike ('rightmost' long vowel) differs from Kondic's '(first) long vowel' attribution to the same paper, which the catalog already notes as a partial disagreement. Nothing from this item remains to be acquired; the primary Larsen & Pike 1949 (JSTOR 10.2307/410088) is still paywalled from our machine per the earlier. The MPI handle landing page (pure.mpg.de item_401934) returned 403 and the SIL site is behind a Cloudflare challenge

sources.note: Theoretical (metrical) dissertation; the Huastec section is a reanalysis of Larsen & Pike 1949 data (Potosino Huastec), not first-hand. It states an unbounded quantity-sensitive system: stress on the rightmost long vowel, else the initial syllable, derived by Weight-to-Stress (right-to-left) plus End Rule Left, with no foot structure and the word as stress domain. The 12 forms in (82) show rightmost-of-two long vowels stressed (bi:nomá:c, hu:čú:k'čik, e:la:šwá:y) and initial stress in long-vowel-less words (cábal, ʔát'em, cálam). sources.citation: Meléndez Guadarrama, Lucero. 2017. Huasteco de El Mamey San Gabriel, Tantoyuca, Veracruz. (Archivo de Lenguas Indígenas de México.) México: El Colegio de México. 194 pp. Open access, repositorio.colmex.mx/downloads/8336h480z.
sources.quote: "Como notaron Larsen y Pike (1949) para el huasteco de San Luis Potosí, el acento en huasteco de El Mamey, Tantoyuca, no es fonológico, es decir, es predecible mediante una regla: en palabras de dos o más sílabas, el acento recae en la sílaba que tiene un núcleo vocálico complejo. Cuando no hay longitud, el acento tiende a recaer en la primera sílaba a la izquierda de la palabra." Examples ['ʔat.em] 'sal', ['ʔol.om] 'cerdo', [ta.'jiːl] 'después', ['k'aː.mal], ['taː.ta], [ta.'taːʔ] 'tú'. (Veracruz/Tantoyuca variety; third variety now independently sourced.)

sources.citation: Herrera Zendejas, Esther. 2014. Mapa fónico de las lenguas mexicanas: formas sonoras 1 y 2. 2a ed. México: El Colegio de México. Cap. 7 'Patrones fónicos del huasteco (ISO hus)', pp.233-281 (Tancanhuitz, San Luis Potosí). Open access, repositorio.colmex.mx/downloads/rb68xf97m.
sources.quote: p.275: "Según los ejemplos de (a) ['ka.le, 'ka.mab, 'pak.laθ], el huasteco no distingue entre las sílabas CV y CVC para la asignación del acento ... las consonantes en coda no contribuyen al peso de la sílaba. El patrón acentual es fuerte-débil, por lo que corresponde a un patrón trocaico. En los ejemplos de (b) [pa.'t'aal, 'kuu.lab, tek'.'θaal, tsa.ma.'maal, wa.'k'aaʃ] apreciamos que la lengua es sensible a la cantidad, ya que si hay una sílaba con vocal larga, ésta atrae el acento." Analysed with moraic trochees; includes duration measurements (2 speakers) showing V: vs V contrast and coda s

sources.note: Largest reference grammar of the language (Potosino); Bennett 2016's 'rightmost long vowel' formulation and his examples [bi:lm'e:l], [mi:ml'a:b] come from it -- the only primary evidence for what happens with two long vowels, which decides 'rightmost' vs Kondic's '(first)'. We hold it only second-hand.
